text:
alisa: Noticing a recurring pattern this week — small capacity dips in eu-west during high-concurrency bursts. Looks tied to older scheduler config + relaxed quota backstop. Verified on 3 different host pools. :thinking_face:

miguel: Can you paste the metric windows? cpu/gpu util, pending queue length?

alisa: Quick snapshot: gpu_util spike to 92% for ~6m, queued_requests up 40% on average, headroom dropped from 18% -> 4% before autoscale kicked. Linked logs: https://redwood.internal/ops/logs/314159

devon: Ugh, those pools still have scheduler_v1 with aggressive packing and no per-tenant soft quotas. We rolled v2 in prod last month but didn't migrate some legacy pools.

ryan: TL;DR: legacy scheduler + no quota guard = slow preemption -> temporary headroom collapse. Sounds like a config migration + quota rule gap.

priya: Proposal: 3 action items — (1) add soft quota guards for user-facing tenants, (2) migrate legacy pools to scheduler_v2 (canary first), (3) add a short soak test each day for surge patterns. Owners? ETA?

alisa: I'll take (1) — add soft quota guards and a metric alert when soft quota usage > 80%. Target: EOD Thu. :white_check_mark:

miguel: I'll drive (2) migration plan. Canary a single eu-west pool tomorrow, rollback-on-error. Estimated finish for staged rollout: next Tue. Will post playbook and rollback steps.

devon: I'll implement (3) — a 10m synthetic concurrent job that simulates peak traffic and verifies headroom >= 12%. Start daily at 02:00 UTC. Will add to the ops-runner schedule.

ops-bot: Reminder: created incident-task ID INC-314159-A for quota-guard; due 2026-04-02.

ryan: Two quick config knobs to consider for v2 (for Miguel):

```
# scheduler_v2 tunables
max_packing_ratio = 0.7  # avoid overpacking latency-sensitive jobs
preempt_threshold_ms = 180000  # reduce preemption lag
```

Let's test these in canary.

priya: Also recommend a short-term backstop: if headroom < 6% for >3m, force route new requests to fallback model tier (smaller/cheaper). That buys time during migration. Who owns policy?

miguel: I'll own the fallback policy too. Can implement routing rule in the next day for eu-west only.

alisa: Cool. Summarizing owners/timelines:
- Soft quota guards: alisa — EOD Thu (3141660000)
- Scheduler v2 canary -> rollout: miguel — canary tomorrow, staged rollout by next Tue
- Daily soak test: devon — start 02:00 UTC daily, implemented today
- Fallback routing rule: miguel — 24h canary

devon: I'll add the soak test job and a quick dashboard panel for headroom by pool.

priya: I'll create a short post-action doc with runbook snippet and add to the incidents handbook.

alisa: Thanks. Small ask: miguel, please add a short blameless note in the migration PR about the telemetry we used so we can spot similar patterns earlier. :memo:

miguel: Will do. I'll post the PR link here when ready.

ryan: One follow-up item: schedule a 30m retro next week to look at recurring patterns across regions (not just eu-west). I'll create the invite.

ops-bot: Task INC-314159-A updated: owner=miguel, status=assigned. Next update due in 48h.

alisa: Great work team. Quick wins + canary -> should reduce recurrence. Ping here when canary completes. :rocket:
